text: Study Sources 1 and 2.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
‘Education is of great importance to our children.’
What are the strengths and weaknesses of the argument supporting this claim?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
‘If we spend more money on education, our children will get better qualifications.’
How could you test this claim? You may consider the types of information, sources of evidence
or methods you might use.

text: Study Source 3.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Identify one prediction from Okeke’s statement.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Identify one opinion from Chika’s statement.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Identify one value judgement from Chika’s statement. Explain why this is a value judgement.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Which argument is more convincing, Okeke’s or Chika’s?
Your answer should consider both statements and you should support your point of view with
their words.
You should also consider:
• the strength of their reasoning and evidence
• their use of language
• the different types of information used.

text: Study Source 4.
Your government wants to improve education for everyone in school. The following areas of
investment are being considered:
• provide more money for school buildings and equipment
• improve the number and quality of teachers
• give rewards to children with good attendance and exam results.
Which one of these actions would you recommend to the government, and why?
In your answer you should:
• state your recommendation
• give reasons to support your choice
• use the material in the sources and/or any of your own ideas
• consider different arguments and perspectives.
